Stewart Barrett's harmonica played the sweetest sounds, always coming in at the right time, unlike "Scrubber" Gordon on his wash-board who came in all the time on the assumption that he would be right some of the time.

Manning, who obviously knows how to feed a hungry athlete, looked after the refreshments, whilst in the bar John Martin did sterling work in ordering the beer, etc., and was ably assisted by Denis MacManus, Jack Carter and Stu.
Left to right - Stuart Barrett, Paul Williamson, John Flynn (obscured), Paul Pringle and Dave Davies.
Stewart Barrett also reaped the efforts of his consistent training of late and here's hoping he continues to improve on this now without any more long lay offs.

And talking of bars - Dennis MacManus, Jack Carter and Stuart Barrett - we couldn't have done without them. These are not just words, without them we could have put up the shutters as far as socials were concerned.
Stuart Barrett just missed the hour with 60:12 (56th) and George Piddington clocked 67:31 (67th). The Isle of Wight Marathon is always a tough event.

Only 'Boofer' and Stewart Barrett now cling leech-like to Brian but he puts in another surge. "Go get the swine, Stew!" Up the hill and along the Ridgway the battle rages until sprinting past the 'King of Denmark' Stewart just gets ahead and holds it into the Club hall.

Stu Barrett has written to draw our attention to John Tee's fine debut in last years Brighton run. John, who turned to running as part of his training for black-belt standard judo, finished in 26th position out of 90+ starters in the excellent time of 6hr 46.03.
